function: Generates BS transmit beamforming vectors and RIS reflection coefficients directly from noisy uplink pilots and user weights to maximize the weighted sum-rate (p. 3, 6)
system: Downlink TDD: BS with 8 antennas (4x2 URA), nearly passive reflecting RIS with 100 elements (10x10), 4 single-antenna users, 1.5 GHz, 20 MHz (p. 5, 9)
method: Hypernetwork (fully connected) generates part of the weights of a beamforming network (FCNN or GNN) from user weights; self-supervised training on weighted sum-rate loss (p. 7-8)
data_channel: Custom simulator: Rician BS-RIS and RIS-user links, Rayleigh direct links, 3GPP TS 38.901 path loss only, random user positions; no dataset (p. 9-10)
test_conditions: 1000 new random test samples; a model trained at default settings is tested across other noise powers and Rician factors (p. 10-12)
baselines: Non-learned: block-coordinate descent with perfect CSI (manifold optimization and WMMSE); learned: static-FCNN, static-GNN2 (GNN of [22]), static-GNN3 (p. 8)
metrics: Average downlink weighted sum-rate (bit/s/Hz) and relative gap to BCD with perfect CSI, versus epochs, pilots, Rician factor, noise power; training and test time (p. 11-14)
complexity: Big-O operation counts for HNB-FCNN, HNB-GNN2, static-GNN3; runtime per realization 1.7 ms and 2.8 ms; training 25.95 h and 25.89 h (p. 14)
q1_support: p. 10: "modeled as Rician fading"; only the path loss follows 3GPP [36], so it is a custom simulator with no 3GPP channel model, ray-tracing data, or measurements.
q2_support: p. 12: "generalizing to data generated using different characteristics or parameters"; Fig. 6c tests one default-trained model across Rician factors 4 to 12 dB, while Fig. 6a and 6b are noise-power sweeps.
q3_support: p. 8: "the GNN of [22]"; static-FCNN and static-GNN3 are other learned baselines, and the non-learned baseline is BCD with perfect CSI (p. 8), all compared on the weighted sum-rate.
q4_support: p. 14: "the proposed HNB-FCNN and HNB-GNN2 required 1.7 ms and 2.8 ms, respectively"; the same section gives the big-O complexity of each scheme.
q5_support: p. 10: "The system and channel model parameters, common across all considered scenarios, are summarized in Table VI"; the channel is a custom simulator, and no code link, data link, or public dataset appears.
notes: Included as area 3: BS beamforming and RIS reflection coefficients are generated from noisy pilots (p. 3). q2 rests on Fig. 6c (p. 12-13); the noise-power panels 6a and 6b are SNR sweeps that do not count, so the reviewer may confirm the Rician-factor test. q1 is not met because only the path loss follows 3GPP TS 38.901 [36] and the fading is custom. The file is the Aalborg accepted manuscript with two cover pages.
